newsitem.title: UK: Syria seen raising Oct light crude price by 10 cts.
newsitem.headline: Syria seen raising Oct light crude price by 10 cts.

text.p: Syria's state oil company Sytrol appears to have stuck to its guns and insisted on a 10 cent rise for its main light crude for October liftings, European traders said.

They said Syria had told term lifters several buyers had accepted the new official selling price for October for its Syrian Light grade. This would take it up to Dated Brent -30 cents from Dated Brent -40 cents for September.

Syria has insisted on getting a higher price for its light sour grade after Algeria raised its October selling price for Saharan Blend, encouraged by Mediterranean refiners' appetite for sour grades in a tight market.
Sour benchmark Urals was offered 10 cents firmer at Dated Brent -65 cents, giving sellers of similar grades incentive to hold out for higher differentials.
Sytrol has not confirmed the price increase and none of the term lifters admitted to accepting the new price but several traders said they believed the price had been set at at that level.
Healthy demand for fuel oil and relatively tight prompt supply of Russian Urals crude has helped to bolster margins for high sulphur grades, traders said.
The price at which Syria's heavier Souedie crude was fixed was not known but Sytrol was offering Dated Brent -$2.90 against bids of Dated -$3.00. Souedie for September was at Dated Brent -$2.85.
